prize_parts.citation: For experimental demonstration and quantitative description of long-range electron tunneling through proteins

statement.case_for: Gray and Winkler showed, with photoinitiated electron transfer in ruthenium-modified cytochrome c, azurin and myoglobin, that electrons tunnel 10-25 Angstrom through protein at rates set by distance, driving force, reorganization energy and the intervening medium. That is a physical mechanism for biological energy conversion stated in measurable terms, and it underlies how respiratory and photosynthetic chains are understood and engineered. The pair is compact and cleanly attributable as the experimental program, decades of independent confirmation exist, and the contribution is chemical in the central sense: a quantitative rate law for a reaction in a biological medium. I accept that it has the weakest opening support on the list, since I am the only member who placed it. That makes the expert reports the right test, and I do not want it dropped just because it did not draw votes.
statement.case_against: Opening support is thin: only my own ranking. The 1992 Marcus prize already covers the underlying electron-transfer theory, so the committee must be satisfied that the protein-tunneling contribution is a distinct achievement and not a corollary. Pathway-model theory (Beratan, Onuchic) and parallel experimental work (Dutton and others) sit outside the credited names, so the citation wording has to carry the priority question. It can also be read as a long line of work and not a single discovery. My closeness to the subject, since my own field is electron and proton transfer in respiratory enzymes, is a reason for others to test my enthusiasm hard.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks targeted protein degradation (B043) second, values it as a new modality, but notes that no PROTAC is approved, that the molecular-glue branch is a separate contribution, and that credit exceeds three people.
responses.response: I agree with his own reservations more than with the rank. The PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito) are two achievements with different protagonists, and a three-person prize would have to cut one of them. He says clinical proof is pending, which is a maturity problem for a prize that cites consequences. I would keep B043 as a serious candidate to revisit, but I do not think it is ready for a clean configuration this year.

responses.point: Linke places halide perovskites (B016) first for a clear physical picture, a fast rise to over 25 percent efficiency and unforeseen opportunities, and also ranks energy landscape theory (B019) fifth.
responses.response: The scientific impact of perovskites is not in doubt, and I ranked it last mainly because it is outside my field. My concern is the one he states himself: six credible names, stability and lead content unresolved, and a priority chain (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, with Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis) that expert reports must settle. On B019 I side with him that Dill is a real competing strand, but I would keep Fersht because phi-value analysis is what tested the theory against experiment, and that connection is what makes it chemistry.

responses.point: Somfai puts Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B052) first for its practical simplicity and decades of use, and ranks PROTACs eighth as too early and lacking a new reaction.
responses.response: His point that degraders are design principles and not new chemistry is a fair qualification, and it supports my caution on B043. For B052 I share his worry about overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize. Maturity is beyond question, but the committee must ask whether a different bond construction with a different ligand logic is a new achievement or a sequel. I would want the expert reports to answer that before ranking it over a discovery that has no prior prize in the area.

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045) first for delivery chemistry that enabled siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, and concedes credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved.
responses.response: The impact is exceptional and the maturity is shown, so I do not dispute the case. My objection is attribution: his own pair (Cullis, Langer) differs from Sparr's trio (Cullis, Hope, Madden), and the two proposals disagree on who is decisive. Until the expert reports establish who developed the ionizable lipid and rapid-mixing formulation and who contributed the broader delivery concept, I cannot tell whether this is a prize of two or of three. The proximity to the 2023 Medicine prize also needs to be handled in the citation.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports will treat protein electron tunneling as distinct from the 1992 Marcus recognition.
Whether pathway-model theorists or Dutton should be included for a fair citation, which the three-person limit and the supplied credited names may not allow.
Whether any configuration with real majority support exists, given that the strongest opening support (B043, B016) comes with unresolved attribution or maturity problems.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Gray, Winkler or any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile. Two points to note: B062 is close to my own research field of electron and proton transfer in respiratory enzymes, which is a scientific closeness and not a recusal ground; and I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose first-place candidate (B001) I do not judge in a way tied to that link.
